description: Hello Everyone! My name is Carlos, and I'm a fourth-year astrophysics student at Saint Mary's University. I am an active student researcher, and I'm super interested in Extragalactic observational astronomy, space missions, and scientific outreach. I have a concrete foundation in physics, mathematics, and programming, but multiple heads are always better than one! Team members with a good foundation in STEM are welcome!
summary: Our team developed a public website that uses NASA's SPHEREx data to display sky images, making it easy for anyone to see the proper motion over time quickly.
details: Our project (InfraRed Information and Analysis System, or IRIS) works by connecting to the NASA Spherex database at the IRSA and using those images to allow users across the globe to make discoveries of celestial objects from IR pictures using time series. We used Python as the backend of the website, which was made with software called Encode. We realized the similarities between our project and Zooniverse, but we wanted to use ours as a pipeline to connect to Zooniverse and enhance citizen science.
